chapter: Learning piano, dancing and Alphonso Trent
title: Moving to Dallas in 1918 and cleaning for a piano lesson
summary: The family moves to Dallas; Price works for a neighbor in exchange for practicing on her player piano and learns 'My Isle of Golden Dreams'.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And I had an opportunity to see Daybreak Nelson, who was a comedian, and some dancers and some singers... early singers of that period. Finally the time came that my mother decided to move to Dallas. She went ahead and got a little house for us and in 1918 we moved to Dallas. Well, I got right off the Inter-Urban and went straight to the Park Theater to find Ella B. Moore. Now I didn't have any idea that Mrs. Moore would have anything to do, Danny, with my playing music. You know, because in those days you were not sure...I didn't know whether I wanted to be a dancer...I couldn't make up my mind...the guy said I couldn't play...he had me paranoid 'cause he said that I couldn't understand anything about music and don't even...you know, so that was a thing that was not discussed in my household. So, one day I was walking up the street. I heard a player piano--by this time now they were in vogue, and popular and-with people had a few dollars, you know, I guess you could buy it now and pay for it later. My brother and I passed this lady's house, and she said, "You boys want to make some money?" My brother said, "No way." you know, he wanted to stay away from work as far as he could. I asked the lady, "Doing what?" She said, "you know, helping me clean the house and raking the leaves and so forth." I said. "I'll take the job if you'll

let me practice on your piano." Just like that. Now, that was my introduction...those were the first words spoken, you know, about the piano. She says, "Okay, some Saturday morning." And I came Saturday morning and I worked hard and finally the time came for me to go into this lady's parlor and sit down at the piano. Well, what I did was to play the piano roll and watch where the notes went down and then sequels like that, and I learned how to play a song called, "My Isle of Golden Dreams." That's how I learned it. And that was her favorite song. And I wore that song out, you know what I mean, I played it everywhere I'd go, you know, in whatever key if they did have a piano--there were two or three people in my neighborhood--Martha Turner & Dave Allen had pianos, see, and I used to go and play that and then I would play it the way [it was] originally and I'd play with a lot of rhythm, you know what I mean, and then just fool around and just improvise and, you know, that was my first introduction to the piano.

Yeah...well later by Mrs. Pittman,, Booker T. Washington's daughter. Later. But my first introduction to the piano was that lady asking me if I wanted to do some work for her. And I said yes. I don't know how that came out of my mouth, "Yes, I will, if you'll

let me play the piano." And then from that, I became big and bold. In 1923 the Charleston dance came out. And I became like an exceptional Charleston dancer. Now doing these dances, Danny, did one thing for me. It taught me to have confidence before an audience.
